articleTitle: Controller design of bidirectional Buck-Boost converter for low frequency pulse power supply
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Low-frequency pulse power supply is mainly used in laser, radar, medical devices, chemical dust removal and vehicle-mounted power supply. Its output is constant voltage and pulse current, so its power is in pulse form. In order to prevent its pulse power from being transmitted to the input terminal, it is necessary to add storage units at the output terminal to compensate the pulse power. Usually, a storage capacitor is connected to the output end of the power supply to compensate the pulse part of the power, but the volume and weight of the output capacitor at this time will be very large. The storage capacitor can be replaced by a parallel bidirectional DC-DC converter to reduce the capacitance volume. The factors that affect the compensation effect of bidirectional DC-DC converter generally include circuit parasitic parameters, circuit topology and control strategy. In this paper, the bidirectional Buck-Boost converter in low-frequency pulse load is selected as the research object, and the controller is designed for this system, so that the system can better track the pulse current when the pulse comes and ends, so that the pulse has less influence on the input current and the output voltage fluctuates less.

articleTitle: EMT Modeling Method for SVG Considering Transient and Steady-State Consistency Verification
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This paper proposes a precise modeling method for Static VAR Generators (SVG) configured in renewable energy stations, taking into account the consistency verification of transient and steady-state conditions. Firstly, the power circuit of mainstream SVG in renewable energy stations is introduced, which is the prerequisite for constructing the electromagnetic transient model of SVG. Then, the typical control structure of SVG is presented, which forms the basis for building the electromagnetic transient model. Subsequently, a parameter identification method for the electromagnetic transient model is proposed, including both steady-state and transient parameter identification methods. Finally, the feasibility and accuracy of the proposed SVG electromagnetic transient modeling method are demonstrated through model verification in both steady-state and transient dimensions.

articleTitle: Multi-objective integrated energy control system that uses compromise programming method
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This paper establishes a mathematical model for the optimal scheduling problem of the P2G-CCS integrated energy system. The model comprehensively optimizes the allocation and scheduling of various energy forms within the IES, such as electricity, thermal energy, and gas, focusing on economic efficiency, environmental impact, and system robustness. The compromise programming method transforms the multi-objective problem into a single-objective problem. During the solution process, the max-min comparison method and fuzzy decision-making are used to select the most suitable compromise solution between economic efficiency and environmental impact. Simulation analysis demonstrates the method’s effectiveness, yielding an optimal compromise solution costing $12,856.3689$ Yuan(Y) and carbon emissions of $\mathbf{1 0, 0 2 0. 2 9 0 8} \mathbf{k g}$. Through optimal allocation and scheduling, the integrated energy system can significantly reduce operational costs and carbon emissions while ensuring the stability and reliability of the energy supply.

articleTitle: A Method of Power Transmission Line Planning for Undeveloped Islands
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Nowadays, there are still many islands in the world that have not been developed. When human beings develop, power construction is an indispensable part of the island development process. To address the problem of high cost of geographical exploration and transmission line planning in the early stage of island power construction, this paper establishes a universal island model and combines the policy iteration algorithm to plan the island transmission line. Finally, the efficiency of the transmission line planning is improved and the labor input of the previous planning is greatly reduced.

articleTitle: Multi-time Scale Stochastic Optimization for Hybrid AC-DC Distribution Networks with PET Based on E-C-Kmeans Clustering
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This paper addresses the uncertainty of distributed power supply in a hybrid AC-DC distribution network with multi-port Power Electronic Transformers (PET). A multi-time scale stochastic optimization model based on E-C-Kmeans clustering is proposed. First, the E-C-Kmeans clustering and reduction model for new energy scenarios is constructed by integrating the CBFSAFODP algorithm (a fast search and density peak discovery algorithm) with the K-means algorithm. Then, the model aims to minimize wind curtailment penalties, operational and maintenance costs of energy storage devices, electricity purchasing costs, and micro gas turbine generation costs. A random optimization operation model for the day-ahead and intra-day scheduling of the hybrid AC-DC distribution network with PET based on E-C-Kmeans clustering is built. Finally, the case study on the hybrid AC-DC distribution network with PET verifies that the proposed model can reduce system operating costs and effectively address the uncertainty in the distribution of renewable energy generation.

articleTitle: Estimating the Power Losses in Induction Motor using Temperature Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: The paper proposes the estimation of power losses in electrical machines using a measurement technique based on the temperature of the electrical machine and the heat transfer equation. To demonstrate this concept, the heat diffusivity of the induction motor can be illustrated through thermal images. This research addresses the impact of supply voltage unbalance on power loss in induction motors. The system comprises A contact temperature measuring circuit utilizing the IC LM 35DZ as a temperature sensor and signal converter, paired with a computer equipped with a National Instruments PCI 6014 data acquisition card. The experiment was conducted by adjusting the phase unbalance to $10 \%, 20 \%$, and $50 \%$ to observe temperature changes. This allows for a direct temperature in the induction motor. The primary advantage of this method is that the machines do not need to stop or be removed from their operational process to measure their losses during preliminary maintenance.

articleTitle: Operation Evaluation of the Green Electricity - Carbon - Green Certificate Market Based on Combined Weight method and Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This paper presents a method for evaluating the operational efficiency of the green electricity, carbon, and green certificate markets, combining the ordinal relationship method, entropy weight method, game theory, and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation. It first establishes a comprehensive assessment index system for these markets, determining both subjective and objective weights using the ordinal relationship and entropy methods. Next, game theory is applied to derive combination weights, and the fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method is employed to assess the operational performance. A case study verifies the applicability and effectiveness of the proposed method, with results indicating that the green electricity market shows strong competition and management efficiency, the carbon market features a stable structure with consistent pricing, and the green certificate market has a solid foundation and growth potential. This research offers a novel approach to assessing the operation of these interrelated markets, supporting their healthy development and contributing to the energy transition and achievement of the “dual carbon” goals.

articleTitle: Research on Key Technologies of Collaborative Spectrum Sensing Based on Differential Privacy
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Aiming at the incentive mechanism issues in collaborative spectrum sensing and access for privacy protection in Internet of Things (IoT) crowd sensing, a multi-task winner selection mechanism based on differential privacy is proposed to address the privacy leakage in Mobile Crowd Sensing (MCS). This mechanism utilizes the exponential mechanism of differential privacy to select winners, protecting the cost privacy information of Crowd Sense Users (CSUs). Furthermore, to incentivize CSUs, a two-layer Stackelberg game algorithm is proposed. This algorithm can coordinate the compensation paid by Secondary Users (SUs) for spectrum access and the data quality reported by CSUs, thereby effectively enhancing the enthusiasm of CSUs to participate in sensing and the performance of collaborative spectrum detection. Simulation results using MATLAB software show that compared to traditional methods, the proposed algorithm increases the average user reward by $19.5 \%$.

articleTitle: Analysis of Operation Effectiveness Evaluation Technique of Power Trading Center Based on Coefficient of Variation Method-TOPSIS Modeling
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the deepening of China's electricity market-oriented reform, the current power market is characterized by large-scale, multi-cycle, multi-subject, and low-carbon power supply, and the power trading center is facing new challenges. In this context, it is very important to improve the operation and management level of the power trading center for the sustainable operation and development of enterprises. Therefore, this paper proposes an evaluation technology for the operation effect of the power trading center based on the coefficient of variation method-TOPSIS model based on the actual operation and management of the power trading center, so as to provide reference and reference for enterprises to reasonably carry out the evaluation of the operation effect and improve the efficiency and effectiveness of operation and management.

articleTitle: Research of UAV inspection system for new energy power stations in special scenarios
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This article explores the key technologies and research of unmanned aerial vehicles in intelligent operation and maintenance of new energy power plants in special scenarios. With the rapid development of new energy power plants, traditional operation and maintenance methods face many challenges in complex terrain and harsh environments. Drone technology, with its flexibility and efficiency, provides new solutions for the operation and maintenance of new energy power plants. This study focuses on analyzing the application advantages of drones in special scenarios, exploring relevant key technologies, and verifying their effectiveness through case studies. The research results indicate that drone technology can significantly improve the efficiency and safety of new energy power plant operation and maintenance, providing important references for the development of future smart operation and maintenance systems.

articleTitle: Research on edge computing capability optimization of intelligent fusion terminal in distribution area based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: For the scenario of multiple edge servers and multiple smart meter devices. First, the system model is constructed, and the problem model is to minimize the weighted total cost of delay and energy consumption. Based on DQN, we integrate Actor network and Critic network into it to form a new DDPG algorithm, which adopts deterministic strategy to select actions by approximating the value function model of neural network. According to the actual problem, three elements are set for the deep reinforcement learning algorithm: state, action and reward. Finally, the calculation time of various migration strategies was recorded. The results show that compared with DQN and other algorithms, the proposed DDPG algorithm can obtain a better task migration strategy, and has a significant effect on reducing the total weighted system overhead.

articleTitle: Enhancing Distribution System State Estimation Using SRGAN-Based Data Interpolation for Load and DER Measurements
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Accurate Distribution System State Estimation (DSSE) is critical for the reliable operation, monitoring, and control of modern distribution networks, ensuring precise estimation of system states essential for maintaining voltage stability and efficient load management. However, the limited temporal resolution of measurement data from smart meters, typically recorded at 30 -minute intervals, poses challenges to achieving high-accuracy DSSE. This paper proposes a novel approach that employs a Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (SRGAN) to upscale low-resolution data for load power consumption and Distributed Energy Resource (DER) measurements into high-resolution data. By capturing finer temporal variations in the measurement data during training process, SRGAN improves the quality of measurements for DSSE, leading to more accurate state estimation. The proposed method substantially improves the quality of high-resolution measurements when compared to linear-interpolated data. By integrating SRGAN-interpolated pseudo-measurements into the state estimation process, the approach achieves a marked improvement in state estimation accuracy over low-resolution data. This demonstrates the strong potential of SRGAN-based interpolation to enhance the precision and reliability of state estimation in distribution networks, offering a promising solution for addressing measurement gaps in modern power systems.

articleTitle: A dynamic fault optimization detection method for cable lines based on Bayesian inference and spectral clustering
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: The cable is a multi-layer structure, and when mixed faults occur, the cable status signal will experience attenuation and distortion. It is necessary to cluster data of different fault types into different clusters, otherwise the packet loss rate will be high and the accuracy will be low. Therefore, a dynamic fault optimization detection method for cable lines based on Bayesian inference and spectral clustering is proposed.Based on the fuzzy Bayesian theory, a scoring function for the operation efficiency of cable lines is constructed, which integrates the characteristic index information of different operating states to analyze the abnormal fuzzy state of cable line data and obtain smooth cable state signals. Based on spectral theory, classify the core point set of cable line data, transform the clustering problem of the core point set into an undirected graph multi-path partitioning problem, complete spectral clustering of cable line data, and control packet loss rate.Using particle swarm optimization algorithm with inertial particles, obtain spectral clustering results with typical dynamic fault characteristics of cable lines, and complete dynamic fault optimization detection of cable lines. The experimental results show that the research method has a very obvious smoothing effect on the original cable status signal, and the clustering results of cable fault data features are very ideal. When completing cable fault detection, the packet loss rate and AUC index are both more ideal.

articleTitle: Research on China’s Inter Provincial Spot Market Clearing Algorithm Considering Bi-directional Trading
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the development of China’s new power system and the large-scale integration of renewable energy, the balance dynamics of the power system have undergone significant changes. This has led to a substantial increase in the demand for short-cycle and frequent adjustments of electricity trading across provinces. Inter-provincial spot trading has emerged as a critical mechanism to enhance the flexibility of inter-provincial markets, playing a vital role in ensuring power security, reliable supply, and the effective utilization of renewable energy. However, the current inter-provincial spot trading framework predominantly relies on unidirectional trading paths and matching transaction methods, which limits its algorithmic capability to meet the evolving demands of the new power system. To address these challenges, this study proposes an optimized inter-provincial spot trading clearing algorithm designed for complex network bidirectional trading. The algorithm incorporates inter-provincial network security constraints and operational conditions, simulates bidirectional trading paths through the construction of a mirror network, and employs a mixed integer linear programming (MILP) approach to solve the optimization problem. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm has been validated using practical examples based on typical daily scenarios, demonstrating its potential to adapt to the complexities of the new power system.

articleTitle: Research on the Construction of Index System and Comprehensive Evaluation Method for the Development Level of New Power System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Scientific and rational evaluation of the development level of the new power system is of great significance for the planning and construction of the new power system. This article constructs an evaluation index system and comprehensive evaluation method for a new type of power system. The construction of the new power system is complex and data intensive, and China is currently in its early stages, lacking a clear evaluation system. This article constructs an evaluation system based on five characteristics: clean and low-carbon, safe and sufficient, economically efficient, supply-demand coordination, and flexible intelligence. It includes 21 secondary indicators and proposes a comprehensive evaluation method based on indicator grading to divide the development level into four levels. Taking three provinces in China as examples, the effectiveness of this method was verified. The research results can provide scientific basis for the planning and decision-making of new power systems.

articleTitle: Mechanical defect recognition method for transmission line structural components based on association rules
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Due to the different mechanical stresses experienced by transmission line structural components, the mechanical defect data after sample cutting and expansion exhibit different characteristics, resulting in overfitting of structural component data and poor positioning performance. Therefore, a correlation rule-based method for identifying mechanical defects in transmission line structural components is studied. Adaptive weighted fusion of multi-source sensing data for transmission line structural components, extraction of mechanical defect edge features through point cloud binary fitting, and overfitting control of transmission line structural component data; Extract mechanical damage feature points, calculate the clustering distance of association rules, and after distance mapping, directly locate the mechanical defect target of the structural component. The experimental results show that this method can effectively fuse data from different sensors, the image peak signal to noise ratio after over fitting control is high, the mechanical defect target location effect of structural parts is better, and the accurate recognition of different types of mechanical defects can be completed.

articleTitle: An improved Transformer with DBB and KAN for smart building energy consumption prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Energy building energy consumption prediction plays a crucial role in energy management and sustainability. While deep learning approaches, particularly Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) like LSTM and GRU, have shown promise in this field, they face challenges in capturing the complex periodic patterns in building energy data. Traditional Transformer architectures, with their simple feedforward network structures and fixed activation functions, often struggle to fully capture the complex interactions among these influencing factors. This paper presents an improved Transformer model for building energy consumption prediction by incorporating three novel components: Diversified Branch Block (DBB), Fine-grained Temporal Extraction module (FTE), and Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN). Experimental results on two real-world datasets demonstrate the model’s effectiveness. On the Belgium dataset, it achieves an MSE of 0.018, MAE of 0.057, and ${\mathrm {R}}^{2}$ of 0.974, significantly outperforming traditional approaches like LSTM, GRU, and standard Transformer. On the BGD2 dataset, the model exhibits robust performance across different building types, achieving MSEs of 0.016, 0.013, and 0.015 with corresponding $\mathrm{R}^{2}$ values of 0.944, 0.953, and 0.962 for educational, office, and residential buildings respectively. Ablation studies confirm the contribution of each component: DBB enhances feature extraction, FTE captures fine-grained temporal patterns, and KAN improves the modeling of nonlinear relationships. The integration of these components produces a synergistic effect, resulting in improved performance in building energy consumption prediction tasks.

articleTitle: Smooth Path Planning for Unmanned Surface Vehicle in Environments with Unknown Polygonal Obstacles
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Path optimization is a critical issue in unmanned surface vehicle (USV) path planning. The smoothness of the generated path and the number of turning points directly affect the ability of the USV to navigate safely. To address the global path planning problem in unknown polygonal obstacle environments, a novel path planning method with obstacle avoidance based on visibility graph is presented in this paper. The polygonal obstacles with different shape are modeled to get a smooth, feasible and collision-free path. The USV only needs to consider the closest obstacle in view and choose the shortest path to the target from the visibility tangent graph formed by the three nodes (its current position, the nearest obstacle, and the target). Upon encountering an obstacle, the USV navigates along the obstacle boundary and transitions to the next tangent path toward the target. The method can effectively reduce the computational complexity and generate a smooth path. The simulation results are consistent with the theoretical values, which verifies the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Analysis of PFC control strategy of voltage stabilizer based on low voltage treatment
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This study addresses the issue of low voltage in rural power grids by proposing a front-end Boost PFC (Power Factor Correction) rectifier with a voltage-doubling structure for a voltage stabilizer. The voltage stabilizer employs two control strategies—average current control and hysteresis current control—to achieve a stable DC bus voltage and high power factor. Through Matlab/Simulink simulations, the study compares various target parameters under these two control strategies. The results indicate that the average current control achieves a lower THD (Total Harmonic Distortion) value of $\mathbf{3. 2 0 \%}$, compared to $4.46 \%$ with hysteresis current control, while both strategies reach a high power factor ($\mathrm{PF}=\mathbf{0. 9 9}$).

articleTitle: Capacity Optimization and Economic Analysis of Off-grid Wind-solar Hydrogen Storage System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: To enhance the economic efficiency and operational stability of off-grid wind-solar hydrogen production systems, a novel capacity configuration method is proposed. This method optimizes system equipment capacity in an integrated wind-solar-hydrogen system with the objective of maximizing system revenue. A case study is conducted using data from a wind-solar hydrogen production project in a specific region, where three schemeswind energy, hydrogen production, wind-battery hydrogen production, and wind-solar-battery hydrogen production-are designed and compared. The analysis reveals that, under the given wind and solar conditions, the system achieves maximum benefit when the wind power to photovoltaic installation ratio is 2.75:1. Additionally, energy storage effectively mitigates fluctuations in new energy output. The study also examines the cost composition of the wind-solar hydrogen storage system and the impact of equipment costs on the unit hydrogen production cost. The findings show that the cost of wind turbine equipment significantly influences the unit hydrogen production cost. A 50% reduction in wind turbine costs corresponds to a $4.9 \mathrm{CNY} / \mathrm{kg}$ increase in hydrogen price.

articleTitle: Optimized Control Strategies for Green Low-carbon Base Station Systems Based on the Energy Router Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This paper explores optimized control strategies for green low-carbon base station (BS) systems within the energy router (ER) framework. It highlights challenges such as rising energy demands and carbon emissions driven by the rapid expansion of mobile communication infrastructure, especially in the 5 G era. The study introduces a two-layer rolling optimization algorithm to enhance energy efficiency through the spatiotemporal management of renewable energy sources and energy storage systems. Key contributions include: A multiport/source architecture integrating photovoltaic (PV) systems, wind turbines, batteries, grid connections, and BS loads. Novel control strategies based on port and load characteristics. Implementation of a rolling optimization mechanism to manage battery charging/discharging under dynamic pricing and varying weather conditions. Simulation results validate the system’s ability to optimize renewable energy use, minimize grid dependence, and improve operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Prediction of ground subsidence surrounding the transmission tower based on BSO-BP neural network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: It is of great significance to accurately predict the variation trend of the ground settlement around the transmission tower, and to take repair and prevention measures in advance, so as to effectively reduce the occurrence of transmission accidents. In view of the lack of prediction accuracy of BP neural network in land subsidence prediction, this paper innovatively introduces a bulnius optimization (BSO) algorithm, which optimizes the initial value of weight and threshold of BP neural network by adaptive adjustment of inertia weight, so as to build a BSO-BP prediction model of land subsidence. Finally, by comparing the predicted results with the measured data, it is found that the BSO-BP model can predict the ground subsidence around the transmission tower very accurately.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Adaptive Inertia Control for Grid-Forming Power System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: As renewable energy sources (RESs) are increasingly integrated into power grids, the power system exhibits characteristics of low inertia and low damping, which significantly impact system stability. Virtual synchronous generator (VSG) technology allows grid-connected inverters to replicate the external behavior of synchronous generators while providing flexible adjustments to virtual inertia, thereby enhancing power system stability. However, the relationship between frequency and inertia is often simplified as a piecewise or linear function, whereas in practical systems, this relationship is typically nonlinear. To tackle this problem, this study initially examines the influence of inertia and damping parameters on system stability using the VSG mathematical model. Then, an adaptive inertia control approach utilizing deep reinforcement learning is introduced to dynamically adjust the virtual inertia of the VSG, thereby improving system stability. Finally, multiple simulation experiments are performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Research on modeling and simulation optimization of multi-energy station based on TRNSYS
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the continuous growth of global energy demand and the increasingly severe environmental problems, multi-energy stations, as a comprehensive energy system integrating a variety of distributed energy forms, have gradually become an important way to achieve low-carbon energy transition. This paper focuses on a typical multi-energy station, constructs its dynamic simulation model based on TRNSYS software, and deeply analyzes the operating performance of the system. Through the simulation analysis of different operation scenarios, the research results show that the interconnected operation of energy stations can significantly save $32.8 \%$ of energy consumption compared with independent operation, and this benefit is mainly due to the staggered characteristics of heat load. The study provides an important theoretical basis for regional energy management and emphasizes the necessity of implementing energy station interconnection according to local conditions to improve energy efficiency and promote the wide application of clean heating.

articleTitle: Application of Large Language Models in Intelligent Preprocessing and Forecasting of Electricity Price
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the gradual liberalization of global energy markets, accurate electricity price forecasting is crucial for effective system operation and market-oriented reforms—especially for emerging Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) that rely on precise market insights. Traditional forecasting methods often struggle to account for the influence of complex unstructured data, such as news events, on price dynamics. To address this challenge, we propose a novel data preprocessing method that leverages large language models (LLMs) to automatically extract, classify, and derive insights from unstructured news articles (sourced from platforms such as WattClarity), which are then integrated with high-frequency electricity price data. To ensure data consistency, a weighted mean algorithm aggregates price records from 5-minute to 30-minute intervals. Our case study on a multi-source dataset demonstrates that this LLM-based technique not only effectively captures critical market signals from textual data—providing a robust framework for supporting market-driven decision-making for VPPs-but also overcomes the limitations of traditional forecasting approaches by harnessing the unique capabilities of LLMs. The integration of unstructured data processing with precise data aggregation underscores the practical advantages of our approach in modern electricity market applications.

articleTitle: Optimization Study of Flexibility Scheduling Strategies for Independent and Interactive Operation of Regional Integrated Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: In today’s increasingly severe energy crisis, integrated energy systems have become an important way to solve the above problems because they can realize multi-energy complementarity and improve energy efficiency. The mathematical model of the integrated energy subsystem and the regional integrated energy system is constructed, and its objective function and constraints are analyzed, and then, based on the example, the data analysis of the operating costs of the multiple systems under the interactive operation mode and the independent operation mode is carried out. The results show that the system can save $6.61 \%$ of the total cost compared with the independent operation, which has better economic efficiency and energy utilization. By considering the changes in the costs of independent and interactive operation of the integrated district energy system at different confidence levels, it is concluded that the interactive operation mode is superior to the individual operation mode at any confidence level.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a New Power System Technology Achievement Recommendation System for Sample Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the rapid development and technological innovation of the power system, the management and optimization of new power systems such as microgrids and distributed energy systems have become a research hotspot. This article introduces the design and implementation of the CRKG-STS model, which is a sample analysis and recommendation system for new power system technology achievements, this system combines matrix recovery technology and collaborative filtering algorithms to achieve real-time analysis of user needs and personalized technical achievement recommendations through dialogue processing, recommendation execution, and knowledge graph module collaboration. By utilizing Relationship Graph Convolutional Networks (RGCN) to enhance entity encoding and employing Transformer architecture for context sensitive text suggestion generation, the accuracy and efficiency of recommendations have been effectively improved. The experimental results show that CRKG-STS outperforms traditional methods in multiple performance indicators, significantly improving user experience and the matching effect of technological achievements.

articleTitle: Research on Dynamic Energy Regulation Algorithm for Hybrid Energy Storage in Large-Scale Island Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the widespread application of renewable energy, improving the regulation efficiency of energy storage systems in island microgrids has become a key issue in enhancing system stability and energy utilization. This paper proposes a dynamic energy regulation algorithm based on a hybrid energy storage system, aiming to optimize the energy management of microgrids by dynamically adjusting the charging and discharging process of storage devices in real-time. The algorithm combines the advantages of lithium batteries and supercapacitors, allowing for dynamic adjustment of the energy storage system’s operation under varying load fluctuations and the uncertainty of renewable energy generation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms traditional methods in terms of regulation accuracy, stability, and energy utilization efficiency, significantly reducing energy losses during the storage process and effectively extending the lifespan of the energy storage system. Furthermore, a detailed comparison of energy storage efficiency and lifecycle under different storage strategies is presented, further validating the effectiveness and economic viability of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Optimal Design and Installation of Solar Rooftop for Thai government building
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This research presents an approach for installing grid-connected solar cells on the rooftops of a prototype building in Thailand to offset electricity consumption, aligning with TOU electricity pricing. It includes design methods, energy-saving calculations, and illustrates the savings from solar cell installation over a one-year period, without accounting for solar cell deterioration or system loss charges. The study compares the concept of installing solar cells on the rooftop based on the building’s electricity usage characteristics, distinguishing between installing solar cells across the entire rooftop area and according to the building’s electricity usage behavior during daytime and working days, ensuring minimal electricity remains while still being sufficient for use. Furthermore, it calculates the comparison before and after installation to provide information for rooftop installation on the prototype building. The research results indicate that installing solar cells across the entire rooftop area can save electricity costs up to 550,000 THB per year.

articleTitle: Stochastic production simulation-based capacity economic optimization study for thermal power flexibility modification
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This paper employs stochastic production simulation to study the economic optimization of capacity for flexible retrofitting of non-heating thermal power units. The research addresses the issue of wind and solar energy abandonment in the “Three North” regions of China due to a lack of system flexibility. To minimize transaction costs for peak regulation, deep peak regulation costs, and system abandonment costs, a flexibility capacity optimization model is developed, considering factors such as reducing minimum stable power, increasing power regulation rates, and enhancing start-stop flexibility of thermal power units. Using data from a regional power grid in northern China, the study finds that flexible retrofitting of large-capacity units is economically optimal. Genetic algorithm is utilized to solve the objective function, demonstrating the model’s practicality. This research contributes to improving the operational efficiency and integration of renewable energy in power systems.

articleTitle: Study on Optimal Configuration and Economic Models of PV Side Cell Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: The randomness and intermittence of distributed photovoltaic power generation lead to low resource utilization. Battery energy storage has the ability of fast power throughput and flexible operation, and is currently one of the effective means to solve photovoltaic grid connection and consumption. This paper studies the current high cost of energy storage and unclear income models, and constructs economic income models of energy storage systems from the perspective of comprehensive income of investors and society. This paper analyzes the cost and benefit composition of energy storage and constructs a life cycle income model of energy storage from the perspective of comprehensive income of investors and society. Use the optimal economic indicators to configure the capacity of energy storage. The breakeven and sensitivity analysis of important factors affecting the economic benefits of energy storage is carried out. Based on the typical day data of a distributed photovoltaic system, the economic analysis and capacity optimization allocation of the energy storage system are carried out. The results show that the cost factor of energy storage plays a major role in the economic benefits of the system.

articleTitle: Optimal scheduling study of active distribution network based on source-load-storage co-optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the transformation of global energy structure and the promotion of China’s “dual-carbon” goal, highproportioned new energy which has been connected to the grid poses a new challenge to the traditional Distribution Network. Active Distribution Network, which can control the combination of various types of distributed energy sources, is an effective means of solving these problem. An active distribution grid optimization and scheduling model with source-load-storage coordination is constructed to maximize the power supply reliability and minimize the operation cost of the distribution grid. Simulation analysis is carried out based on the IEEE-33 node system, and the results show that the optimized scheduling strategy significantly reduces the amplitude of load fluctuation, alleviates the peaking pressure of the Distribution Network, and improves the flexibility and regulation capability of the system.

articleTitle: Maximum torque-to-current ratio control of permanent magnet synchronous motor parameters under differentiated operating conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This study focuses on the Maximum Torque per Ampere (MTPA) control strategy for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSM) in electric vehicles under diverse operating conditions. By conducting an in-depth analysis of the PMSM mathematical model and integrating voltage and current constraints, a control method based on extremum equations for MTPA is proposed. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively reduces energy consumption across all speed scenarios, with particularly notable improvements under low-speed and high-acceleration conditions. Compared with the traditional control, the energy consumption per unit mileage is reduced by $7.58 \%, 3.12 \%, 3.17 \%$ and $2.37 \%$ in the speed zones of $35 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}, 50 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}, 70 \sim 100 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ and $100 \sim 120 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$, respectively, and the motor loss is optimised, which provides both theoretical and practical support for the enhancement of energy efficiency of electric vehicle drive motors.

articleTitle: Research on Dynamic Maintenance Model of Multi subsystem Wind Power Generation Based on SAPSO
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: A dynamic maintenance strategy based on Simulated Annealing and Particle Swarm Optimization (SAPSO) for Multiple subsystems of Wind Power Generation (MSWPG) is proposed to address the issues of high maintenance costs and low reliability in wind power generation under complex operating conditions. Firstly, a study was conducted on the nonhomogeneous Poisson continuous life distribution model based on reliability functions and life distribution functions, and the commonly used basic MSWPG maintenance models were analyzed. Then, based on the Markov decision model, the dynamic maintenance strategy of MSWPG was modeled, and the maintenance strategy of multiple subsystems was optimized based on SAPSO, improving maintenance efficiency and operational stability. Finally, the dynamic maintenance strategy of the proposed MSWPG was validated through experiments in the event of faults in the generator system, wind turbine system, pitch system, and frequency conversion system. The experimental results show that the average cost of the proposed optimization strategy is $\yen 3860 /$ day, $\yen 3620 /$ day, $\yen 2970 /$ day, and $\yen 3040 /$ day, respectively, which is lower compared to traditional methods. The average returns are $\yen 13750 /$ day, $\yen 14260 /$ day, $\yen 15320 /$ day, and $\yen 14720$ /day, respectively, with reliability rates of $92.63 \%$, $\mathbf{9 3. 5 6 \%}, \mathbf{9 2. 8 5 \%}$, and $\mathbf{9 3. 3 7 \%}$, which is a significant improvement compared to traditional methods.

Author Keywords: Multiple subsystems of wind power generation

articleTitle: Transient Stability Enhancement Control for SLVM-Controlled Virtual Synchronous Generators via Hybrid Integral Gain Swithcing and Active Power Compensation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This paper performs a large-signal analysis of Virtual Synchronous Generators (VSGs) with single-loop voltage magnitude (SLVM) control. Phase-portrait analysis reveals that the integral gain of SLVM affects transient stability. To address the trade-off between transient stability and steady-state performance, a hybrid control strategy combining SLVM integral gain switching and integral gain-based active power compensation is proposed. The extended equal area criterion (EEAC) is employed to analyze virtual kinetic energy variations, elucidating the mechanism by which the integral gain influences transient stability. Simulation and experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy, demonstrating improved synchronization and faster post-fault recovery.

articleTitle: Introduction of application of rapid location of line short circuit fault in low voltage transformer district
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Based on the software and hardware resources of the existing intelligent devices in the low-voltage transformer district, this paper introduces the comprehensive application of key technologies such as the physical topology of the distribution area lines, fault indication, local communication, and fault location, so as to realize the automatic and rapid location function when short-circuit faults occur in the low-voltage transformer district lines. Through the analysis on the main technical links, the operating parameters, communication mechanism and equipment coordination mechanism are determined to improve the reliability of the operation of the automatic and rapid location function when short-circuit faults occur in the low-voltage distribution area lines. The scheme is based on the existing equipment upgrading software, which greatly reduces the equipment investment. Through the automatic location of line short-circuit fault, it can reduce the manpower and material resources investment in the process of line short-circuit fault maintenance, shorten the maintenance time, and has great engineering value.

articleTitle: Lithium-Ion Battery Fault Early-Warning Method Based on DTW-DBSCAN
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: In light of the pervasive utilization of lithium-ion batteries across diverse domains, concerns regarding their safety and reliability have gained significant prominence. We put forward a research methodology for the development of an early warning system for lithium-ion batteries, underpinned by the principles of Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) and Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN). DTW effectively addresses the issue of inconsistent time scales caused by charging and discharging processes, environmental factors, etc., and can accurately capture subtle changes in the operating state of lithium-ion batteries. DBSCAN, based on the density of data points, flexibly identifies different pattern clusters in lithium-ion battery operation data, thus distinguishing between normal and abnormal operating states of different levels. The research proposed in this paper provides novel concepts and methodologies for the safety monitoring and early warning of lithium-ion batteries, thus offering a foundation for the preventive maintenance of battery safety.

articleTitle: New energy power prediction of microgrid based on optimized SVM
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the increasing emphasis on renewable energy worldwide, the stable operation and efficient management of microgrids have become particularly important as platforms for integrating and optimizing new energy sources. New energy generation, such as wind and photovoltaic power, is intermittent and uncertain, posing challenges to power balance and scheduling within microgrids. To effectively address these challenges, this paper proposes a new energy power prediction method for microgrids based on Support Vector Machine (SVM). The study begins by analyzing the characteristics of new energy power generation, including the fluctuation patterns of output power from photovoltaic and wind sources, as well as their main influencing factors. Next, the SVM prediction model is constructed, utilizing historical data of new energy generation and its influencing factors as inputs. This model leverages the nonlinear mapping and regression analysis capabilities of SVM to accurately predict future power output. For model construction, radial basis function (RBF) is employed as the kernel function, and model parameters, including the penalty factor and kernel function parameter, which are optimized using cross-validation and grid search methods to enhance prediction accuracy and generalization ability. Experimental results demonstrate that the SVM-based new energy power prediction method achieves high prediction accuracy, providing robust decision support for power balance and scheduling in microgrids.

articleTitle: Study on the control strategy of load-side converter in wind-solar storage off-grid power supply system
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This paper studies the control strategy of the DC/AC converter on the load side of the grid-connected photovoltaic system, aiming to solve the challenge of load fluctuations on system stability. An improved control algorithm is proposed to address the shortcomings of the traditional VF control strategy, which significantly improves the response speed and accuracy of the system to sudden load changes, thereby ensuring voltage and frequency stability. MATLAB simulation results show that the improved control strategy can effectively cope with sudden load changes, stably maintain system voltage and frequency, and ensure the reliability of power supply.

articleTitle: A Data Collection and Transmission Method for Smart Meters Based on Homomorphic Cncryption
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the rapid development of smart meter technology, how to ensure the privacy and security of power data has become a key issue in smart grid systems. This paper proposes a hierarchical energy metering data collection method based on homomorphic encryption. This method uses time segmentation and homomorphic encryption technology to enable each branch meter to securely encrypt its electricity data and upload it to the upper meter. The upper meter obtains the electricity data of each branch meter by decrypting its known total current information, while the branch meters and attackers cannot decrypt the specific data of other meters. This method ensures the privacy isolation between branch meters and improves the security of data transmission. At the same time, it also has good flexibility and topological adaptability, can adapt to the needs of multi-level, distributed power networks, and is particularly suitable for the application of large-scale smart grid systems. Through experimental verification, the method in this paper can efficiently complete data encryption, transmission and decryption while ensuring privacy security, has strong anti-attack capabilities, and can reduce system operation and maintenance costs.

articleTitle: Application of Bayesian-based Distributional Robust Optimization in Wind and Solar Power Output Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: In order to clarify the variability of renewable energy generation, this paper proposes using Bayesian multivariate nonlinear models and Bayesian nonlinear interaction models to describe the power uncertainty of wind and solar generation, based on distributionally robust optimization methods. The wind and solar output for typical scenarios are then calculated. Finally, the variations in wind and solar output under different confidence levels are analyzed.

articleTitle: Research on a New Power System Achievement Retrieval and Recommendation System Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Addressing the challenge of traditional methods in handling big data and providing precise information in power systems, this study develops a novel power system achievement retrieval and recommendation system leveraging deep learning. The system enhances traditional methods with user behavior-based algorithms, a new deep learning model for efficient literature search, and unsupervised clustering for faster sorting. It integrates user patterns for personalized recommendations, improving retrieval efficiency, accuracy, and user service in tracking power system advancements.

articleTitle: Multi-scale detection method of power lines suitable for complex scenarios
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Transmission lines, as an important component of the power system, play a crucial role in delivering electrical energy from power plants to users. With the continuous expansion of the power system and technological advancements, the accuracy and efficiency of transmission line detection have become increasingly important. Traditional image processing methods have achieved some success in simpler backgrounds, but in complex backgrounds or low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) environments, they face challenges such as low accuracy and poor anti-interference performance. To address these issues, this paper proposes a transmission line detection algorithm based on feature keypoints. Instead of using traditional pixel-based segmentation, this method employs keypoints to represent the geometric features of transmission lines. By considering the local structure and geometric features of the target, the method effectively improves detection accuracy. To further enhance performance in low SNR environments, a global dual-attention mechanism is introduced. The spatial attention mechanism focuses on key regions in the image, while the channel attention mechanism adaptively adjusts the importance of different features, thus enhancing the model's feature extraction capability. This is especially effective in detecting long, thin transmission lines. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms traditional methods in complex environments and can detect transmission lines more accurately, offering significant practical value and innovation.

articleTitle: Study on ecological environment impact and soil and water conservation technology of power transmission and transformation projects in typical ecologically fragile areas in western China
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Along with the development of the West Power Transmission and Transformation Project, how to reduce the effect of the project on the ecological vulnerable region and adopt the effective measures to protect the soil and water has become an urgent issue. A model is designed to forecast the environmental and ecological effects of power transfer and reconstruction projects based on machine learning and genetic algorithm. People can forecast the effect of power transfer and transformation project on soil erosion and vegetation destruction based on the random forest algorithm. The results indicate that the soil erosion rate is increased by $25 \%$, and the vegetation cover is reduced by $15 \%$, and the soil erosion is reduced by $30 \%$, and the vegetation is recovered by $18 \%$. Through this model, the decision maker can get more precise EIA data in the planning phase, which will provide the scientific foundation for the coordinated development of ecoprotection and project construction.

articleTitle: A Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Strategy for Optimizing V2G Energy Scheduling on Supply and Demand Sides
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the rapid development of new energy vehicle technology, there is a need for vehicle-to-grid (V2G) as energy management and storage. In this study, a novel V2G scheduling method using the Deep Q Network (DQN) algorithm is introduced, aiming to optimize the charging and discharging usage needs of both V2G supply and demand, while jointly reducing the operating costs of the grid and electric vehicle users. The suggested approach tackles the issues of high-dimensional state-action spaces in V2G systems by the integration of a dual learning mechanism and a priority replay method. A V2G experimental platform was established utilizing real city grid data, incorporating 100 electric vehicles, and the method was assessed under diverse load circumstances and levels of renewable energy integration. The results indicate a $\mathbf{1 5 \%}$ enhancement in peak shaving on the demand side and a $10 \%$ decrease in user expenses relative to traditional rule-based approaches, concurrently improving system stability. This study offers a significant theoretical and technical foundation for the implementation of smart energy management in vehicle-to-grid applications.

articleTitle: Conditional WGAN-GP-based Renewable Energy Scenario Generation Method
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: As the proportion of renewable energy in the power system continues to increase, the uncertainty of its output poses huge challenges to power system planning and dispatch. A renewable energy scenario generation method based on the Wasserstein GAN with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) is proposed. WGAN-GP effectively solves the problem of unstable training in traditional Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) by introducing conditional information, and can generate more diverse and representative scenarios. Verification was carried out using the GEFCom 2014 dataset. The results show that this method shows superior performance in terms of accuracy, autocorrelation and comparison with traditional methods such as Markov chains. This research provides a new solution for the generation of renewable energy scenarios and has broad application prospects.

articleTitle: Solution Research on Distributed Photovoltaic Energy Storage Output Strategy
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This article provides a concise analysis of the current limitations in PV systems and suggests improving the feasibility of engineering applications through the integration of energy storage devices, thereby establishing a distributed photovoltaic storage system model. Utilizing historical load and photovoltaic data from a company in South China, the study employs optimization programming software to achieve operational economic optimization on a typical day. Furthermore, it explores the economic advantages of the distributed photovoltaic storage system over an extended time scale in practical engineering scenarios.

articleTitle: Low-Carbon Photovoltaic and Energy Storage Configuration for Highway Service Areas Based on Multi-Objective Traffic Energy Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: To enhance service quality, many service areas have introduced fast-charging stations for electric vehicles (EVs). However, these stations often demand substantial charging loads, primarily supplied by traditional energy sources, leading to increased carbon emissions and costs. Therefore, establishing a low-carbon, economical, and energy-efficient energy supply system for highway service area charging stations has become imperative. This involves optimizing the configuration of photovoltaic (PV) systems and energy storage to minimize carbon emissions while maximizing economic benefits and clean energy utilization.In constructing such a low-carbon, economical, and clean energy supply system for highway service area charging stations, this study proposes an integrated PV and energy storage optimization model that considers comprehensive energy efficiency. The model aims to achieve multiple objectives: minimizing carbon emissions, reducing annual operational and investment costs, and maximizing energy self-sufficiency. Constraints include the charging and discharging states of EVs. Given the discrete and discontinuous variables, along with multiple objectives in the established model, the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III) is employed for optimization.Case studies demonstrate that, within a microgrid model of a highway service area charging station, the system meets EV charging and discharging demands and basic load requirements. This results in improved service levels, reduced carbon emissions, and enhanced power supply reliability. The proposed model is also applicable to other service area charging stations. Integrating a high proportion of renewable energy into the grid can effectively achieve clean, low-carbon, and economical energy supply.

articleTitle: Transient Flow Analysis of a Turbine Cover Drainage System Based on TransAM
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: The turbine cover drainage system of a certain hydropower station may experience a siphon effect during operation due to its unique pipeline layout. This study utilizes TransAM, a Canadian complex fluid computational pipeline network software, to model and conduct transient flow analysis of the drainage system. The impact of the siphon effect under different operating conditions is explored. For hydropower stations where the siphon effect is severe, it is recommended to consider air valve optimization at the design stage by installing air valves at the highest points of the drainage pipelines for each generating unit. This ensures the safe and stable operation of the drainage system. The findings of this study provide strong support for the optimization of the turbine cover drainage system and serve as a valuable reference for siphon protection design in similar engineering applications.

articleTitle: Thermal-Electric Coupling Simulation Analysis of Battery Busbar
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the advancement of new energy technologies, busbars in battery systems, as critical connecting components, play a vital role in system safety and efficiency. This study establishes a thermal-electric coupling model theory and response surface method for busbar, employing ANSYS Fluent software for simulation analysis to evaluate temperature variations under different operating conditions. The results indicate that under variable current charging, and constant voltage charging conditions, the highest temperatures of the Al busbar all occur at the central connection sections and remain within safe limits. Under the extreme melting current charging condition, the melting current of the Al busbar is approximately 734 A, with an error rate of $1.8 \%$. This research provides theoretical support and simulation methods for the design and selection of Al busbar, holding significant theoretical and practical implications.

articleTitle: Research on the planning and operation of integrated energy systems with hydrogen storage systems
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the increasing integration of renewable energy into power grids, modern power systems face unprecedented challenges in operational flexibility and stability. Integrated energy systems (IES), as a pivotal support component for these systems, enhance renewable energy absorption while ensuring secure and reliable operation. To further exploit the active support potential and operational flexibility of IES, this study establishes a hydrogen energy storage-based IES optimization model. The model prioritizes economic efficiency as the primary objective function under energy balance constraints and equipment operational limitations. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed hydrogen-integrated planning model ensures reliable electricity and heat supply, reduces carbon emissions, and improves renewable energy absorption capacity.

articleTitle: Optimized Scheduling of Heating System Electrical Load Using an Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm Considering Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimized scheduling strategy for renewable energy-based heating in Inner Mongolia, aimed at improving economic feasibility and meeting heating load demand. The proposed strategy aims to meet electricity supply requirements while maximizing economic benefits and minimizing environmental impact. First, a control strategy for the renewable energy heating system is developed, and a wind-solar-storage hybrid system model is constructed. Next, considering the volatility and uncertainty of wind and solar power, a power system simulation is conducted using the IEEE 33-node distribution network, incorporating heating load demand. The power variation data of each device, ensuring compliance with the voltage requirements of the distribution network, is used as the initial input for the optimization algorithm. Lastly, a multi-objective optimization scheduling model for grid-connected microgrids is proposed, integrating operational and environmental costs, and solved using an improved particle swarm optimization algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on traffic prediction model for power communication optical network based on deep learning joint optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the rapid development of energy transformation and digital technology, the surge of massive distributed energy access, interconnection between data centers under the electric computing collaboration scenario and other new power services have put forward unprecedented needs and challenges to the communication network, and the new era of optical transmission network as the base of arithmetic power needs to solve the problem of large capacity and low latency. Therefore, this paper analyzes the characteristics of traffic data in optical transmission networks and constructs a time series to predict network traffic through neural networks, and the simulation results show that the time series model established in this paper can achieve higher prediction accuracy compared with other comparative schemes.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Prediction and Maturity Assessment of Water Electrolysis Hydrogen Production Technologies Based on LSTM-SVR and TRIZ Theory
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Water electrolysis is key to clean hydrogen production, yet its technological evolution remains uncertain. This study applies LSTM-SVR modeling on patent data and TRIZ S-Curve analysis to predict the 15 -year trajectory of ALK, PEM, SOEC, and AEM. Results show LSTM-SVR outperforms single models, accurately capturing trends. AEM and PEM are emerging as mainstream technologies, SOEC remains nascent, and ALK is maturing with declining market share. These findings provide scientific guidance for R&D, policy, and industry strategy.

articleTitle: The Monitoring Layout Method for Distributed Photovoltaic Resources Based on Multivariate Feature Clustering
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Gaps remain in the regional monitoring of distributed photovoltaic (PV) generation resources, with no widely - accepted monitoring plan currently in place. Existing monitoring locations, predominantly founded on past experience and equidistant point distribution, overlook regional spacing and the economic cost of monitoring. An optimized monitoring scheme put forward in this paper, which combines clustering features and optimal location search, takes into account the distribution characteristics of photovoltaic power generation and the consistency of local meteorological resources while averting redundant monitoring, thereby being able to ensure comprehensive data coverage, high representativeness of the selected points, and optimal economic benefits.

articleTitle: Analysis of Single-phase-to-ground Fault Based on Primary and Secondary Integration Circuit Breaker
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Single-phase-to-ground fault (SPGF) in power distribution system (PDS) with neutral non-effectively grounded(NNEG) is a typical multiple fault, and long-term operation with faults may cause overvoltage problem of the entire system, resulting in equipment damage, etc. Based on the characteristics of SPGF, this paper theoretically analyzes the characteristics of SPGF in neutral ungrounded systems(NUS) and resonant grounding systems(RGS), and analyzes the threshold action value setting rules for zero sequence voltage and zero sequence current of primary and secondary integration circuit breaker(PSICB). Finally, based on a SPGF handling case, the application effect of PSICB in handling grounding faults was analyzed.

Author Keywords: power distribution system with neutral non-effectively
primary and secondary integration circuit breaker

articleTitle: REMTCN-Informer A Hybrid Approach to Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: As the focus on photovoltaic (PV) energy intensifies due to its role in clean energy production, accurate forecasting of PV power generation has become crucial. The inherent volatility and complexity of photovoltaic energy output pose considerable challenges to the forecasting task, particularly when dealing with long-term correlations and considering multiple influencing factors such as weather fluctuations over time. This necessitates the development of highly accurate and adaptable forecasting models to comprehensively address and analyse these complex and changeable factors. To tackle these issues, this paper introduces a novel hybrid model, REMTCN-Informer, which synergistically integrates TCN with the Informer model. The REMTCN-Informer model incorporates a range of sophisticated technologies, including residual connection and normalisation mechanisms. These have been shown to enhance the accuracy and stability of photovoltaic power prediction. The experimental results demonstrate that the model exhibits excellent performance across all forecasting time periods. In comparison to traditional forecasting models, the REMTCN-Informer model demonstrates superior forecasting ability and robust performance.

articleTitle: Research on the Coordinated Scheduling Method of Distribution Network Considering Flexible Loads
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the increasing proportion of flexible loads in distribution networks, this paper establishes the dispatching models of electric vehicles, energy storage, electric boilers and incentive loads in distribution network dispatching; establishes the optimization objective and constraints of distribution network coordinated dispatching that comprehensively considers the suppression of new energy access, peak shaving and valley filling, and the safe and economic operation of distribution networks; studies the solution strategies for the above large-scale complex dynamic programming problems, and proposes a distribution network coordinated dispatching method considering flexible loads; Taking the power grid of Dalian, Liaoning Province, China as an example, an application analysis was conducted.

articleTitle: Analysis of Asymmetric Influential Factors through Simulink in Photovoltaic Power on New Energy Grid Connection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This study addresses the pressing challenges of environmental pollution and energy shortages by exploring the integration of renewable energy sources, specifically wind and photovoltaic (PV) power, into the grid. The manuscript presents a detailed analysis of the asymmetric influences, such as temperature and illumination intensity, on renewable energy systems, and proposes a methodology to optimize power output through Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) techniques. Utilizing Simulink simulations, the study models and tracks the power generation of PV cells under varying environmental conditions, examining the effects of temperature and light on system stability and power efficiency. Key findings demonstrate that MPPT effectively stabilizes voltage and current outputs, improving the efficiency of energy transfer, while the system shows promising responses to fluctuations in illumination and temperature. The research emphasizes the importance of integrating renewable energy technologies into the grid to enhance energy security, reduce transmission losses, and minimize the impact of grid failures. This work contributes significantly to the optimization of grid-connected renewable systems, promoting economic growth and reducing reliance on traditional energy sources.

articleTitle: Research on a new power system achievement recommendation method based on attention mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the increasing complexity of the power system, accurate prediction has become crucial for industry scheduling and operation. Traditional methods are inadequate in addressing nonlinear challenges, while deep learning combined with attention mechanisms provides higher accuracy. This article proposes a new performance recommendation method for power systems based on attention mechanism, which integrates convolutional neural network (CNN) and gated recurrent unit (GRU) to achieve short-term load forecasting. By introducing attention mechanism, the model can focus on key data features, extract the core part of time series information, reduce noise, and improve learning efficiency and interpretability. In addition, this article also explores the combination of Bayesian Personalized Sorting (BPR) and attention mechanism for the design and implementation of group recommendation algorithms, considering group project interaction, user project interaction, and group composition. The experimental results show that the proposed ANBGR (Attention based Neural Bayesian Group Recommendation) algorithm has significantly improved recommendation accuracy and normalized cumulative loss compared to other recommendation algorithms.

articleTitle: Vibration reduction optimization of transmission tower-line system based on different control schemes
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: A three-dimensional finite element model of a double circuit transmission tower-line structural system is established and validated in this study. Based on the Kaimal wind speed spectrum and considering spatial multi-point correlation, the fluctuating wind speed time history of the transmission tower-line system is simulated. On this basis, four vibration control schemes are proposed using viscous dampers. The vibration control effects of acceleration, base shear force, and member axial force on the double circuit transmission tower-line structure system are studied based on the four control schemes. The results show that the finite element model constructed can well reflect the dynamic characteristics of the transmission tower-line system, with an error of only $5.5 \%$ compared to the theoretical analysis. The simulated spectrum of fluctuating wind speed matches well with the target spectrum, and the fitting of fluctuating wind speed has good reliability. Under different wind vibration control schemes, good vibration control effects are achieved, and the control effect gradually increases with the increase of the number of viscous dampers and the damping coefficients. Considering the wind vibration control effect and installation & maintenance factors, it is recommended to adopt scheme $\mathbf{C}$ as the optimal control scheme.

articleTitle: Power load forecasting based on Time convolution network and bilstm optimized time series algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This paper discusses the optimal time series algorithm based on time convolution network (TCN) and bidirectional long-term and short-term memory network (bilstm), in order to improve the accuracy of power load forecasting. Through comparative experiments, we evaluated three different models: a separate time convolution network, a bidirectional long-term and short-term memory network, and a bidirectional long-term and short-term memory network optimized by a time convolution network. The experimental results show that the optimized model performs best on the training set, and its root mean square error (RMSE) is 22.26, which is better than using bilstm (RMSE is 24.12) and TCN (RMSE is 29.08) alone. In the test set, the optimized model also performed well, with RMSE of 27.03, while the RMSE of TCN and bilstm were 29.22 and 33.59, respectively. These results show that the bidirectional long-term and short-term memory network optimized by time convolution network has significant advantages in capturing the complexity and dynamics of power load time series. In addition, the evaluation parameters of the model further confirm the superior performance of the proposed model in power load forecasting. It can not only predict the change of power load more accurately, but also better understand and simulate the behavior mode of power system. Therefore, this study not only provides an effective algorithm for power load forecasting, but also provides a new perspective and method for time series analysis in related fields.

Author Keywords: Two way long-term and short-term memory network

articleTitle: Research on Electricity-Cooling Energy Systems for Data Centers: A Case Study of Qingyang
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
