abstract: This study focuses on the synergistic use of electricity and cooling energy within data centers, integrating photovoltaic, wind power, air conditioning, electricity and cold storage. Firstly, a model for renewable energy based electricity and cold energy supply has been established, using the economic index as the objective function, with energy and power balances serving as constraints, and incorporating actual data from Qingyang of China as boundary conditions. Secondly, the model is solved by the mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) in Gurobi to determine the minimum net present value of cost and the optimal scales of its components. Finally, a comparative analysis reveals that compared to configuring electricity or cold storage alone, the coordinated configuration of both of them can significantly improve economic performance. This proposed scheme outperforms the current schemes in Qingyang, with a cost per kilowatt-hour of electricity of 0.3529 yuan $/ \mathrm{k W h}$.

articleTitle: Scenario-Generation-Based Optimal Scheduling Method For Combined Wind-Photovoltaic-Pumped Storage
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Aiming at the combined wind power-PV-pumped storage optimal scheduling problem, firstly, based on the k-means algorithm improved by the elbow method, the daily scenarios of wind and solar power are clustered to generate the typical planning scenarios; then, based on the generated scenarios, the optimal scheduling model of the combined generation system is established with the objective of minimizing the deviation of the grid power of the combined generation system from the demand of the electric power system, and solved by the Black-winged kite algorithm. pumped storage co-generation system optimization scheduling model, and solved by Black-winged kite algorithm. Finally, simulation verification is carried out to prove the correctness and effectiveness of the methodology in this paper.

articleTitle: A Method for Load Synchronization Detection of Power Secondary Cables Based on BeiDou Timing Data
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Conventional power secondary cable load synchronization detection method is based on the load frequency band characterization, and does not take into account the influence of harmonic interference, and the detection results are biased. Therefore, a power secondary cable load synchronization detection method based on Beidou timing data is designed. Detecting the load synchronization variable time sequence of power secondary cable, detecting the load abnormality of a continuous univariate or multivariate time sequence, ensuring the comprehensiveness of load detection. Based on the BeiDou time series data synchronization to locate the abnormal load interval of the secondary cable, using the signal of BeiDou satellite navigation system, the scattering parameters of the secondary cable are determined, and they are used as the observation quantity of the abnormal load combination to avoid the problem of the load synchronization detection error. Using comparative experiments, it is verified that the method has better quality of synchronous detection and can be applied in real life.

articleTitle: Application of Fiberoptic Differential Protection in Ship Lock Power Supply System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: The power supply system of the ship lock represents the core of the ship lock operation. In light of the increasing demand for reliability, the original system protection method has proven to be inadequate in meeting the electrical safety requirements of the ship lock. Fiber optic differential protection offers a high level of sensitivity, robust anti-interference capabilities, and the ability to respond to disturbances at full line speed, making it a safe and reliable short-distance power supply line protection mode. This paper combines the ship locks power supply system protection and transformation process of fiber optic differential protection analysis, describes the practical application of fiber optic differential protection method, and through the fault test situation analysis summarizes the advantages and disadvantages of fiber optic differential protection. It then puts forward the use and improvement of the proposal, with a view to providing guidance and reference for the design of similar projects in the future.

articleTitle: Development of a Magnified Photovoltaic System with IoT Based Tilt Angle Corrector
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Several researchers used Concentrators to focus sunlight onto smaller areas, enhancing power generation and improving the performance of PV systems. In this study, the main objective is to develop a magnified photovoltaic system with a desired tilt angle corrector. The developed system used a magnifying glass to concentrate sunlight onto the PV Panel and integrated it with a cooling system. The system also utilized a Dual-Axis Solar Tracking system to correct the Tilt Angle of the PV Panel. The researchers gathered data from two different months with different altitudes. The developed system was compared to the Fixed PV Panel in terms of Current, Voltage, and Power output and results show that for the months of September and October, the Magnified PV system gained $11.56 \%$ and $12.47 \%$ respectively.

articleTitle: Study on Medium-Term Optimal Dispatching Method of Power System with High Proportion of New Energy Based on Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the rapid development of various new energy sources, the load change of the power system becomes more complex. In view of the complexity of load changes, this paper proposes a medium-term optimal scheduling method based on load forecasting for a high percentage of new energy power systems. First, a load prediction method based on deep learning is proposed. Then, a recurrent scheduling model based on load forecasting is constructed, combining the time correlation among thermal power, wind power and photovoltaic units to establish a recurrent scheduling model with internal and external double cycles. Finally, the accuracy of the load forecast was verified by comparing the load profiles, and the loop scheduling model was analyzed using the improved IEEE 24-node system. The results show that the predicted loads obtained using the deep learning model can be well used for optimal scheduling, and the scheduling results of the system are more in line with the actual changes.

articleTitle: Power Optimization Scheduling Strategy for Multi-Household Energy Management System Considering Load Aggregators
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the widespread penetration of distributed photovoltaic power generation on the user side, the popularity of independent photovoltaic systems for homes makes the demand for optimal scheduling of home energy management systems increasingly prominent. However, due to the small scale of power consumption and insufficient flexible load capacity, it is difficult for single household users to efficiently consume photovoltaic power generation and participate in the demand response of the power market. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-household power cooperative optimal scheduling model considering load aggregators, which integrates scattered demand response resources of small and medium-sized household users through load aggregators, establishes a comprehensive scheduling framework aiming at economic optimization, coordinates multi-household photovoltaic power generation, energy storage equipment and flexible load resources, and introduces a subsidy mechanism to encourage users to participate. Through the analysis of examples, the model significantly reduces the cost of power consumption for household users and the cost of power purchase for load aggregators through the centralized optimal scheduling of load aggregators, and realizes the flexible interaction and efficient utilization of user-side resources.

articleTitle: Site Selection for Pumped Hydro Energy Storage (PHES) Based on the Largest Hydropower in Indonesia’s Five Main Islands
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: As Indonesia moves towards a renewable energy future, finding reliable storage solutions is crucial due to the intermittent nature of solar and wind power. Pumped Hydro Energy Storage (PHES) stands out as a practical option, allowing excess energy to be stored when demand is low and used when it is high. This study focuses on identifying the best locations for PHES across Indonesia using geospatial analysis tools like Digital Elevation Models (DEM) and Geographic Information Systems (GIS). By evaluating factors such as rainfall patterns, terrain suitability, and infrastructure availability, the study identifies key locations that can support PHES development. The largest hydropower site from five biggest islands in Indonesia was selected for the analysis, namely Sigura-gura, Saguling, Riam Kanan, Larona, and Genyem. The GIS model result suggested the largest PHES system at Larona dam with 616.58 MWh stored energy and the smallest site is in Papua with zero suitability due to Genyem Hydropower run-of-river characteristic. However, based on the evaluating factors, the Sigura-gura dam is deemed as the most suitable site for PHES. The findings highlight the role of PHES in making Indonesia’s power grid more stable and efficient as it transitions to renewable energy.

articleTitle: Demand response and renewable generation with optimization approach for energy management in smart grids
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Rising electricity demand and the integration of renewable energy generation (REG) have led to increased variability in the daily load profile, posing significant energy management challenges. Smart grids (SGs), with their advanced demand response (DR) mechanisms and REG integration, offer promising solutions to these issues. This study presents a multi-objective optimization approach to schedule energy consumption for energy management in REG integrated SGs, targeting reducing operating expenses, decreasing emissions, and optimizing user comfort. A probability density function (PDF) is employed to model REG with greater accuracy. The proposed framework leverages the multi-objective fishswarm optimization algorithm (MOFSOA) to identify globally optimal solutions effectively. The findings indicate that MOFSOA with DR excels in simultaneously optimizing cost, emissions, and user comfort, outperforming solutions without DR and offering a robust strategy for sustainable and efficient energy management in SGs.

articleTitle: Optimization Strategies for Environmental Durability of Lithium Niobate Modulation-Based Fiber Optical Current Transducers
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: The optical circuit of fiber current transformers is prone to aging under long-term outdoor exposure to high/low temperatures and humid-heat environments, leading to decreased measurement accuracy or even failure. This paper proposes an innovative design scheme for lithium niobate modulation voltage closed-loop control. It introduces optimization strategies including high-strength integrated waveplate sensing fiber drawing process, sensing fiber winding process with magnetic leakage protection, and temperature compensation algorithm using $2 \pi$ reset technology. These strategies significantly improve the temperature characteristics and consistency of fiber current transformers, achieving a temperature coefficient better than $0.05 \%$ and linearity better than 0.98 across the full temperature range. The proposed high-strength integrated waveplate sensing fiber utilizes polarization-maintaining fiber with gradient spiral structure to replace waveplates, transforming concentrated polarization conversion of cut-type fiber waveplates into gradient polarization conversion. This optimization enhances the vibration response and durability characteristics of lithium niobate modulated fiber current transformers, meeting error limit requirements without installing butterfly springs and buffer washers.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Method for Reconfigurable Distribution Network Based on Intelligent Switches
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Building a new type of power system is a key measure for the energy and power industry to promote the national carbon peak and carbon neutrality strategic goals. In the future, there will inevitably be a high proportion of clean energy sources such as distributed photovoltaics and small hydropower, as well as new types of loads such as energy storage and electric vehicle charging stations, which will be connected to low-voltage distribution networks. The current low-voltage distribution network is located at the end of the entire power grid, with characteristics such as wide distribution, complex power supply and consumption environment, and difficult operation and maintenance. This article forms a distribution network reconstruction architecture based on intelligent switches, with primary and secondary fusion of column mounted switches, lowvoltage smart switches, photovoltaic grid connected switches and other products as the core, forming a flexible and flexible grid structure with low-voltage local balance, medium voltage platform area mutual assistance, and main station comprehensive control. Based on this, a multi-level fault analysis and protection architecture for low-voltage distribution networks is proposed. Through the combination of intelligent switch current difference discrimination and expert knowledge base, precise protection for low-voltage distribution networks is achieved.

articleTitle: Research on fault prediction and diagnosis of smart grid based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of accuracy and real-time fault prediction and diagnosis of smart grid, this paper proposes a fault prediction and diagnosis method based on deep learning. By constructing a deep learning model to extract and analyze the characteristics of power grid operation data, the accurate identification and location of fault types are realized. A fault prediction model based on multi-layer neural network was designed, and a complete fault diagnosis system was established by integrating time series data analysis methods. Experimental results show that the proposed method improves the accuracy of fault prediction by ${1 5 \%}$ and shortens the fault location time by ${3 0 \%}$ compared with the traditional method, which has strong practical value. The research results provide new technical support for the safe and stable operation of smart grid.

articleTitle: Transmission tower icing prediction model based on random forest
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: The icing of transmission lines will cause serious accidents such as broken lines and tower collapse, which will affect the safe operation of the power grid. It is necessary to predict the icing thickness of transmission towers in order to warn in advance. In this paper, the correlation between the icing phenomenon of the transmission tower and the stress of the component is analyzed by finite element analysis. It is proposed to use the component stress and meteorological data as the characteristic quantities to establish a prediction model of the icing of the transmission tower based on random forest. Finally, through comparative verification and analysis, the icing thickness prediction method proposed in this paper can accurately predict the icing thickness of transmission towers and provide theoretical guidance for the safety of transmission towers.

articleTitle: Optimization Strategies for Wind Power Overhaul Considering Probability of Equipment Failure
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Wind turbine failure may produce a large security risk to the power grid, overhaul is a necessary means to eliminate equipment failure. The current overhaul strategy exists in the lack of security and economy and other problems, based on this, a wind power overhaul strategy optimization method is proposed. Under the condition of power market, considering power limit loss, downtime loss, operation and maintenance cost, with the goal of lowest total maintenance cost, and considering various safety maintenance constraints, a wind power maintenance optimization model is established and solved by Ivy algorithm. A wind farm in Gansu is used as an object for simulation and analysis, and the results show that the model proposed in the article can effectively reduce the total overhaul cost and improve the production safety.

articleTitle: Multi-Stage Energy Storage Configuration Method Considering the Evolution Path of New Energy Penetration
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Under the impetus of the “dual-carbon” goals, the rapid increase in new energy penetration has imposed higher demands on the flexibility and economy of power systems. Traditional static planning methods struggle to adapt to the dynamic evolution of new energy and the iterative technoeconomics of energy storage. To address this, this paper proposes a multi-stage collaborative planning method for wind-thermalstorage hybrid systems. First, based on the logistic growth model and learning curve, the evolution of new energy penetration under different policy scenarios is quantified. Second, a mixedinteger linear programming model is established to optimize the economy by coordinating the intertemporal coupling of energy storage lifecycle costs, thermal power retrofitting costs, and peakvalley arbitrage revenue. Simulation results from a case study in a large-scale new energy base in Northwest China demonstrate that the proposed multi-stage planning reduces typical daily total costs by 37.89% compared to static planning, while thermal coal costs decrease by 1.16%. This research provides an economically viable decision-making framework for energy storage temporal planning and thermal power transition in high-penetration renewable energy systems.

articleTitle: Potential of PV and Wind Energy-Based EV Charging Stations to Minimize Peak Load Demand
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: The increasing demand for electric vehicles (EVs) presents a challenge for electric utilities during peak load periods. To overcome these challenges demand response (DR) and time-of-use (ToU) pricing strategies are used, however, they disrupt user routines and make them less attractive. This study investigates the potential of integrating solar and wind energy-based EV charging stations as a solution to minimize peak load demand. The study considers a case study at the beach location of Brisbane, Australia. The case study considers the installation of 2 MW of solar and 1.2 MW of wind capacity. Results demonstrate a $45 \%$ reduction in grid energy consumption, with contributions of ${2 4 \%}$ from solar and $20.9 \%$ from wind energy. Additionally, the system achieves a $41 \%$ reduction in carbon emissions, significant cost savings, a $19.0 \%$ return on investment, and a 4.18-year payback period. Moreover, the energy cost is also reduced from 0.373 ${\$}$ / kWh to 0.256 ${\$}$ / k W h. These findings highlight the effectiveness of renewable energy in reducing peak load demand and associated costs while offering a sustainable solution for EV charging infrastructure.

articleTitle: A BCM Soft Switching Method with Fixed Switching Frequency for Three-level T-type Inverter
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: The three-level T-type inverter is widely used in renewable energy generation applications due to its excellent performance. In order to achieve higher efficiency, the T-type inverter can be controlled to operate in boundary conduction mode (BCM), thereby achieving soft switching to reduce switching losses. However, this approach requires continuous variations in switching frequency, resulting in a complex control strategy and challenges in filter design. This paper proposes a BCM soft switching method with a fixed switching frequency for a threelevel T-type inverter, which enables the inverter to achieve soft switching under pulse width modulation (PWM). The feasibility of the proposed method is verified through simulations of a gridconnected T-type inverter.

articleTitle: Data Anomaly Detection in Modern Transmission Grids Based on GRU-Attention-VAE
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the increasing proportion of renewable energy in power grids and the growing frequency of climate changes, traditional power system state estimation methods tend to misidentify sudden load changes as anomalies, thereby affecting the quality and speed of decision-making in subsequent energy management tasks. Conducting research on anomaly detection techniques for the power dispatch cloud to adapt to the multi-source nature, long time-scale, and high timeliness requirements of dispatch cloud data holds significant application value. This paper proposes a deep learning-based anomaly detection algorithm for electrical data. The model integrates the weakly supervised learning of Variational Autoencoders (VAE), the temporal feature extraction of Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), and the cost-effective extraction of core rules/characteristics in complex systems enabled by the Attention mechanism. The effectiveness and accuracy of the algorithm are verified through case studies, and comparisons with baseline algorithms demonstrate its cost-effectiveness.

articleTitle: Facilitating developments of solar PV power and onshore wind power generations for decreasing carbon emissions in China: A study based on evolutionary game theoretic method
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This article examines encouraging close collaboration between wind and solar power producers and power-consuming businesses and luring outside investment through market mechanism optimization in the face of frequent wind and solar power curtailments. We start by reviewing studies on financing tactics and sales channel restructuring in wind and solar power projects. Then, using wind and solar power plants and energy investment firms as the primary bodies, we build a three-party evolutionary game model and perform theoretical and numerical-example evaluations. The study demonstrates that a number of factors influence wind and solar power facilities’ choices about their sales channels: (1) They often sell electricity to the grid as annual total power generation rises. (2) They prefer to work directly with businesses for long-term supply since energy investment organizations invest more money overall each year. (3) They are more willing to sell to businesses if the grid-selling price increases. (4) Wind power plants tend to improve grid cooperation when the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) rises.In addition to providing fresh policy-making insights, our investigation of the new market mechanism for wind and solar power facilities offers a strong theoretical and empirical foundation for the best market model given Chinese national circumstances.

articleTitle: Research on the Design and Application of ‘Solar+Air’ Energy Hot Water System in University
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Under the background of the strategic goal of ‘ 3060 double carbon ‘, it is urgent for renewable energy to replace traditional energy for energy supply<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>. This paper takes the dormitory building of a university in Jinan as the research object, expounds the working principle of the ‘ solar energy + air energy ‘ dual energy hot water system, and calculates the collector area, the head and flow of the circulating pump, and the heating capacity of the air source heat pump. At the same time, the energy saving benefit of the system is calculated and analyzed. The results show that the application of the system in college dormitories has a good energy saving and environmental protection effect.

articleTitle: Research on Dynamic Reconfiguration Method of New Distribution System Network to Enhance New Energy Carrying Capacity
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the continuous development of clean energy, a large number of distributed generation (DG) sources are connected to the distribution network, and the compatibility of the distribution network with renewable distributed energy sources has led to the diversification of optimization objectives. This paper first analyzes the impact of DG connection location and capacity on the distribution network based on a typical distribution network system. Then, a distribution network reconfiguration model is constructed. Considering the reliability and economy of the distribution network, a genetic algorithm is used to optimize the network reconfiguration structure and DG output, achieving a balanced distribution of energy across all branches. Finally, based on the IEEE33-node system, three typical scenarios with different DG connection capacities are considered to verify the effectiveness of the model.

articleTitle: An Integrated Knowledge Distillation Framework for Battery SOH Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: State of health (SOH) estimation plays an important role in Battery Management Systems (BMS), especially in electric vehicles (EVs). However, deploying deep learning-based SOH estimation models in EVs is challenging due to their large computational demands and model sizes. Moreover, battery datasets often contain environmental noise, which affects the accuracy of predictions. We propose an integrated knowledge distillation (KD) framework for model compression. Under this framework, the size of the model is compressed by knowledge distillation. This framework uses the Wasserstein distance to solve the extreme value problems during the knowledge distillation process. Additionally, we refine Wasserstein distance with a Gradient Penalty (G-P) technique. This method controls the gradients of the model outputs within a certain range, which can solve the gradient explosion or disappearance problems. The experimental results indicate the validity of our framework.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Criteria for Unbalanced Protection of Hybrid Filter Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: To detect internal component damage faults in capacitors, the hybrid filter needs to be equipped with capacitor imbalance protection as the main protection reflecting such faults. However, when capacitors experience intermittent discharge from the shell due to capacitance, traditional unbalanced protection based on power frequency fundamental waves takes too long to operate, resulting in severe equipment damage. Furthermore, the first application of hybrid filters in engineering requires urgent research on the adaptability of existing protection criteria. This article proposes a novel capacitor unbalance protection scheme and verifies the effectiveness of the criterion through simulation experiments. The protective device based on this principle has been tested by a third party and has been put into operation on site with good performance. The research results of this article have certain reference value.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Multi-layered Luminescent Solar Concentrator with Inorganic Phosphors on Solar Windows
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Since the 1970’s, Luminescent Solar Concentrators (LSCs) have been studied. A part of the photons emitted by the Sun will enter the LSC module, which is then absorbed by the luminescent phosphors in the LSC, then redirected and spread out to the edges of the LSC module. Once redirected it the photons can be collected and converted by Photovoltaic cells to generate power. Roughly $25 \%$ of the photons directed at the LSC is lost and absorbed by the module due to Reabsorption Loss. With having a multilayered design for the LSC Reabsorption Losses can be minimized. Using PVTrace simulations the behavior of photons inside a Multilayered LSC is observed and an optimal thickness for the phosphor layer is $\mathrm{2 . 1 5 m m}$ for a multilayered LSC measuring 104x104x19mm. Phosphor layers measuring $0.65,1.15$, 1.65, 2.15, 2.65, 3.15, 4.00 mm was simulated in PVTrace with 100,000 photons each and the reabsorption losses are $24.57 \%$, ${2 4 . 3 8 \%}, {2 4 . 1 8 \%}, {2 4 . 0 3 \%}, {2 4 . 1 6 \%}$ and ${2 4 . 4 8 \%}$ respectively. The phosphor layer measuring 2.15 mm is used for the lower reabsorption losses. Both the single layered and multilayered LSCs have eight (8) photovoltaic cells connected in a series. In the span of 3 hours of actual testing the results showed that the single layered LSC have an efficiency of $4.69 \%$ and the multilayered LSC have an efficiency of ${4 . 7 2 \%}$. The results shows that LSC having multiple layers can improve the performance of an LSC.

articleTitle: Research on the Development of Key Technologies in the Hydrogen Energy Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: The hydrogen energy industry is experiencing rapid development. This paper analyzed the current status and trends of technology development in key links of the hydrogen energy industry, including hydrogen production, storage and transportation, refueling, and application. Fossil fuel-based hydrogen production, industrial by-product hydrogen, and electrolysis of water are the main methods of hydrogen production currently, each with its own advantages and disadvantages. In terms of storage and transportation, technologies such as high-pressure gaseous hydrogen storage, low-temperature liquid hydrogen storage, solid-state hydrogen storage, and organic liquid hydrogen storage have their unique characteristics and are suitable for different scenarios. As the infrastructure for hydrogen energy application, hydrogen refueling stations exhibit diverse construction forms and technical routes, providing strong support for the promotion of hydrogen-fueled vehicles. The application fields of hydrogen energy are extensive, covering transportation, electricity, industry, and other sectors, demonstrating its significant potential as a clean energy source. However, the hydrogen energy industry still faces challenges such as technical bottlenecks, high costs, and inadequate infrastructure construction. This paper aims to provide references for the sustained and healthy development of the hydrogen energy industry and offer theoretical basis for relevant enterprises and government departments to formulate development strategies.

articleTitle: Self-Adaptive Loss Weighting for Improving Multi-Appliance Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) is a technology that identifies the operational status and power consumption of individual electrical devices (typically household appliances) from aggregated smart meter readings. This paper introduces a self-adaptive loss weighting strategy aimed at improving the performance of a single deep neural network-based NILM model for disaggregating multiple appliances. The proposed technique adaptively balances the contributions of each appliance, preventing performance biases toward high-power or frequently operating devices. Additionally, we design and implement a multi-appliance adaptive Autoencoder framework to evaluate this mechanism. Experimental results on the REDD and UKDALE datasets show improvements in disaggregating the power consumption of multiple appliances.

articleTitle: Practical Study on Low-Carbon Energy-Saving Renovation of 220kV Operational Substation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This study investigates the low-carbon renovation of a 220 kV operational substation in Guangzhou, focusing on analyzing electricity consumption patterns, identifying energy-saving opportunities, and validating renovation strategies. Through optimized operation of air conditioning, ventilation, and lighting systems, equipment upgrades, and the integration of photovoltaic (PV) power generation, the substation achieved significant reductions in energy consumption and carbon emissions. The findings provide actionable insights and theoretical support for the green transformation of operational substations, advancing sustainable development in the power sector.

articleTitle: Analysis of Carbon Emission Assessment of Automotive Products Based on Life Cycle Assessment and Suggestions for Low Carbon Development
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: The “Double Carbon” goal puts forward new requirements for the development of the automobile industry. Carbon neutralization in the automobile industry is a systematic project, which requires not only technological breakthroughs in the industry itself, but also carbon reduction in collaboration with other relevant industries. Evaluating the carbon emission level of automobile products with different technology routes has become a research hotspot under the existing technology level and energy structure. Based on the product life cycle assessment, a carbon emission model is built and several comparable models of the mainstream technology routes are selected so as to evaluate their carbon emission throughout the life cycle objectively. The research results show that, Battery Electric Vehicle (BEV) is one of the most important technology routes for the low-carbon development of automobile products at present and in the future. Finally, suggestions for carbon reduction in the life cycle of automobile products are put forward such as developing energy-saving technology of traditional energy vehicles, promoting low-carbon development in all aspects of power batteries, expanding the proportion of clean energy applied in vehicles, improving the green level of vehicle materials, and promoting green low-carbon transformation of production and manufacturing.

articleTitle: Research on Guangxi Smart Substation Project Investment Prediction and Influencing Factors Based on XGBoost-SHAP
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: As an important component of the power system, substations undertake the crucial task of ensuring the safe operation of the power grid, and the annual construction investment is huge. Controlling the investment in substation engineering construction can effectively reduce the costs of power grid enterprises and maximize the efficiency of resource allocation. Based on the feasibility study investment data of Guangxi Power Grid’s smart substation projects in the past three years, this paper conducts an exploration. The principal component analysis method is used to select 11 main features that affect the investment level of substations, and the k-means clustering algorithm is utilized to optimize the sample data set. An index system of influencing factors for the investment in Guangxi smart substation projects is constructed, and an investment prediction model for smart substation projects based on XGBoost is established. Through case studies, the effectiveness of XGBoost in substation investment prediction is verified. Finally, combined with the SHAP values, the influence degree of each feature on the prediction model is obtained, which verifies the validity and applicability of the prediction model. It provides an important reference basis for reasonably controlling the investment in Guangxi substation projects and also offers strong support for investment decision-makers in making investment decisions regarding substation engineering construction.

articleTitle: Short-term Load Forecasting of Photovoltaic Distribution Grid Electricity Considering Carbon Emission Costs
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: In the load feature extraction stage, the traditional methods only consider the power load data itself, while ignoring other factors that may affect the load, resulting in the extracted features are not comprehensive enough, which leads to the low accuracy of the load prediction results. Therefore, a short-term load forecasting method for photovoltaic (PV) distribution network considering carbon emission cost is investigated. Historical load data of PV distribution networks are collected, and the data are filled with missing values, outliers are eliminated, data are normalized, and random noise is eliminated. Considering the influence of carbon emission cost, the Pearson correlation coefficient is used to screen the carbon emission cost features that are highly correlated with the historical load of photovoltaic distribution grid electricity, and the optimized feature set is combined with the convolutional neural network model and exploratory factor analysis method. Considering the characteristics of historical load data and the influence of carbon emission cost, the short-term load prediction model based on the long and short-term memory network is established, and the load features are extracted as inputs, and the short-term load prediction results of the photovoltaic distribution grid are outputted by the forward-propagation operation through the recurrent sub-network of the memory block of the model. The experimental results show that the research method can make the short-term load prediction curve of PV distribution network maintain high consistency with the actual curve, with high prediction accuracy, and the RMSE value is significantly better than that of the comparison method, which effectively improves the prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: The Application of Intelligent BIM Technology in the Management of Low-Voltage Distribution Network Projects
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: With the continuous increase in China's electricity demand, the number of low-voltage distribution network projects is also growing. To ensure that these projects are advanced efficiently, with high quality and in an environmentally friendly manner, it is particularly important to explore effective management strategies. Against this backdrop, BIM (Building Information Modeling) technology, with its excellent data processing capabilities, efficient collaboration mechanisms, and powerful intuitive display functions, has gradually emerged in the field of power grid infrastructure construction, bringing innovative solutions for the refined management of low-voltage distribution network projects. This paper focuses on the management process of low-voltage distribution network projects, delving into the core features of BIM technology and its applications in project management. It also analyzes the significant advantages of BIM technology in improving management efficiency, based on existing research. In addition, this paper points out the current shortcomings of BIM technology and the management of low-voltage distribution network projects, and looks forward to future development directions.

articleTitle: Scalable Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading System With Microgrid Coalitions
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Widespread deployment of distributed renewable energy sources fosters the research and development of peer-topeer (P2P) energy trading systems. Despite the benefits this energy-sharing paradigm can bring to the stakeholders in modern energy systems, how to effectively facilitate energy trading among a large number of energy prosumers (producers-and-consumers) remains a non-trivial challenge. This paper proposes a new P2P energy trading system to support energy trading among prosumers located in geographically distributed microgrids. Backboned by a clustering mechanism that dynamically organizes the microgrids into multiple coalitions, the system can enable energy trading within a microgrid and among different microgrids, making it scalable to cater for the energy trading needs of widearea prosumers. Numerical simulation is conducted on an IEEE 33-bus benchmark distribution system to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Policy Simulation Research on Carbon Market and Green Certificate Market —Based on the CGE Model
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: The simulation of the economic and social impacts of carbon emission trading and green certificate trading systems is a significant concern in light of their current deployment. An “energy-policy” module that integrates the advantages and disadvantages of such policies into a computable general equilibrium (CGE) is presented in this paper. The effects of selling carbon emissions and green certificates are simulated using a computable dynamic general equilibrium model of China’s energy market. The findings show that the economy, carbon pricing, green certificate prices, and power costs are all impacted differently by different carbon emission reduction targets.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Ensemble For Day-Ahead Probabilistic Forecasting of Electric Vehicle Charging Load
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Electric vehicles play a key role in advancing the transition to clean energy. Accurate uncertainty quantification of charging stations, as essential infrastructure for the large-scale adoption of electric vehicles, is crucial to ensuring the stability of the distribution grid. This paper proposes a novel nonparametric probabilistic forecasting approach to address the increasing volatility in user demand at charging stations. Initially, electric vehicle charging sessions are represented as time series data through a classification-based segmentation model, from which features such as the number of concurrently charging vehicles are extracted. Subsequently, we make deterministic predictions using homogeneous and heterogeneous ensembles based on DBN and Bi-LSTM, respectively. The prediction error distribution, derived from feature similarity metrics, is then aggregated to generate preliminary quantile results. Finally, the probabilistic forecasting results are obtained via a stacking ensemble approach, with IQRNN serving as the meta-learner. The day-ahead forecasting experiments conducted on charging sessions from an individual station in California verify the superior performance of the proposed two-stage ensemble approach, compared to single models or similarity-based methods.

articleTitle: Power System Risk Assessment Considering Wind-Solar Output Correlation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: The large-scale incorporation of wind and solar energy presents notable difficulties for maintaining the stable operation of power grids. Due to similarities in regional climates, the output from wind and solar generation often shows a significant degree of correlation, which is essential for the scheduling and risk analysis of power systems. This study utilizes a non-parametric kernel density estimation approach to model wind and solar generation output, effectively capturing their variability. The Copula function is then employed to describe the correlation between wind and solar power outputs, and a Copula-based technique for modeling wind-solar output correlations is introduced. Using Monte Carlo simulations and K-means clustering algorithms, typical wind-solar generation scenarios are created. Through scenario analysis, this research builds a risk assessment framework that incorporates wind-solar correlation, developing an indicator system that focuses on two main factors: voltage violations at nodes and power flow violations in lines. Finally, an IEEE 33-node system is utilized for validation of the case study. The results indicate that the proposed risk assessment method, which accounts for wind-solar output correlations, provides a more accurate reflection of the real operational risks in the power grid, offering a valuable tool for power system scheduling decisions.

articleTitle: Optimisation of Transmission Tower Sensor Arrangement Based on Fisher Information Matrix-Effective Independence Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: The transmission tower sensor arrangement scheme plays a very crucial role in aspects such as transmission tower monitoring efficiency and monitoring accuracy. However, traditional sensor arrangement methods often rely on experience and lack scientific and systematic nature. On this basis, this paper proposes a sensor arrangement optimization method based on Fisher Information Matrix-Effective Independence Method (FIM-EI). With the objective of maximizing the Fisher information matrix determinant of monitoring data, the method fully considers the effective independence between sensors and the redundancy of monitoring information to achieve the optimization of sensor arrangement. Firstly, the Fisher information matrix of the transmission tower monitoring system is constructed to describe the relationship between the sensor arrangement and the monitoring performance; secondly, the sensors contributing more to the monitoring performance are filtered by the effective independence method, which reduces the redundancy of the sensor arrangement; and a sensor arrangement scheme that guarantees the monitoring performance and reduces the cost is obtained. This study provides a new idea of sensor arrangement optimization in the field of transmission tower monitoring, which has certain theoretical value and practical application prospect.

Author Keywords: Fisher information matrix - effective independence method

articleTitle: Probabilistic Forecasting-Based Operational Security Region for Power Systems With Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources (RES) introduces high uncertainty and poses significant challenges to operational security in power systems. This paper proposes a novel probabilistic operational security region (POSR) model for high-penetration RES in power systems, which is based on non-parametric probabilistic forecasting to quantify RES uncertainty. The POSR model provides a local equivalent approximation of RES feasible region incorporating system operational constraints, thereby enhancing computational efficiency in high-dimensional spaces. An innovative POSR-solving algorithm is also developed, leveraging region credibility hyper-box settings and convex hull boundaries to rapidly iterate boundaries. Case studies based on IEEE 33-bus and 141-bus systems validate the effectiveness of the proposed POSR model with high computational efficiency.

articleTitle: A Bio-Inspired Hybrid Optimization Model for Enhancing Operating Performance and Efficiency of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) are critical for the advancement of sustainable transportation, however, there is still a need to optimize energy consumption, battery longevity, and system adaptability. In this study, we introduce Quantum-BioNet (QBN), a hybrid optimization framework that combines quantum computing principles and bio inspired algorithms to address these issues. For efficient exploration of a vast solution space, QBN utilizes parameterized quantum circuits; for real time responsiveness, it uses bio inspired adaptation. The model allows critical EV parameters to be dynamically optimized (i.e., energy management and regenerative braking) under varying operational conditions. Implemented in a MATLAB/Simulink simulation environment replicating real-world scenarios, QBN achieved significant performance improvements: 1) ${2 0 \%}$ decrease in energy consumption; 2) ${3 0 \%}$ increase in battery life; 3) fast adaptation within 5-6 seconds to changes in traffic density and road grade. QBN was found to have better computational efficiency (90 seconds to converge in a computer with ${6 0 \%}$ CPU and 950 MB memory) than state-of-the-art Quantum Optimization (QO) and Bio Inspired Optimization (BIO) algorithms, outperforming QO and BIO by $25 \%$ and $18 \%$, respectively. The results indicate QBN’s capability to revolutionize EV optimization with a scalable, energy efficient and cost-effective solution. QBN combines quantum parallelism and adaptive bio-inspired strategies to implement intelligent and green mobility systems that meet critical requirements of real-world EV operation and accommodate future progress.

articleTitle: Research on Configuration Optimization of Distributed Energy Systems under Demand Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: As energy and environmental challenges intensify, distributed energy systems (DES) are gaining attention for their high energy efficiency. In this study, Latin Hypercube sampling (LHS) technique was used to generate load uncertainty data, and two-stage stochastic programming (TSSP) model was used to optimize device capacity configuration. The research shows that the battery capacity and air conditioning capacity of the system increase after load uncertainty is taken into account, and the cooling load demand satisfaction rate increases significantly. Although the LHS approach resulted in a ${1 4 . 1 6 \%}$ and ${5 . 2 5 \%}$ increase in initial investment and operating costs, respectively, the number of hours that were not met with cooling load requirements was significantly reduced by ${9 2 . 0 9 \%}$, resulting in improved system stability and economy. Although the annual cost increased by $6.58 \%$, the LHS approach effectively coped with load fluctuations. Future research could explore deep learning and reinforcement learning techniques to improve the efficiency and accuracy of scene generation.

articleTitle: Evaluation Index System and Evaluation Method for the Effectiveness of Electricity Substitution
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Electricity substitution is a key strategy for promoting energy transformation and reducing environmental pollution. A comprehensive evaluation of the effectiveness of electricity substitution allows grid companies to make objective judgments about the current level of substitution programs and also provides direction and decision-making for related policymaking. In this paper, firstly, the index system of electric energy substitution effectiveness covering economy, low carbon, safety, and interaction is constructed; secondly, the Analytic Hierarchy Process(AHP) and entropy method are used to determine the weights of the indexes, and the objective and subjective weights are fused and updated through mathematical planning, and the evaluation method uses a combination of the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution(TOPSIS) and matter-element extension evaluation model; lastly, the analysis of examples is carried out by taking the five electricity substitution projects of Tianjin as the objects of the study to verify the practicality, scientificity, and effectiveness of the evaluation system.

articleTitle: ShapeDiff: A Universal Source-Load Time Series Anomaly Detection and Imputation Model
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: The rapid proliferation of sensors in modern power systems has generated vast time-series datasets that are rich in critical operational information. To maximize the utility of these datasets and support the development of high-quality pre-trained models, it is crucial to implement efficient preprocessing methods that effectively address both anomaly detection and data imputation. This paper introduces ShapeDiff, a novel integrated framework that addresses anomaly detection and imputation inefficiencies within time-series preprocessing. ShapeDiff combines shapelet-based anomaly detection for enhanced stability and interpretability with diffusion model-based imputation to ensure superior performance and adaptability to non-stationary data. A self-supervised parallel training strategy facilitates the efficient processing of large-scale datasets while maintaining inference consistency. Experiments demonstrate that ShapeDiff achieves efficient anomaly detection, provides accurate and reliable imputation for common source-load time series, and significantly improves preprocessing efficiency.

articleTitle: Combined Use of Hybrid Optimization and Quantum-Enhanced Neural Evolution for Predicting Cost and Charge Dynamics of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: This paper introduces EcoSwarm, a bio-inspired hybrid optimization algorithm aimed at enhancing cost efficiency and charge management in electric vehicle (EV) fleets. EcoSwarm leverages Quantum-Enhanced Neural Evolution (QENE), which integrates quantum computing principles with neural evolution to significantly improve prediction accuracy and operational efficiency. Unlike traditional optimization methods, EcoSwarm employs quantum-inspired probabilistic transitions to explore a broader solution space, increasing the likelihood of achieving global optimal solutions. The proposed approach demonstrates $\mathbf{3 5 . 6 \%}$ reduction in operational costs and achieves $\mathbf{9 2 . 1 \%}$ energy utilization efficiency—surpassing the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA) by at least 11.3% and $15.8 \%$, respectively. Furthermore, EcoSwarm enhances charging demand prediction accuracy by $32 \%$, as measured by the Mean Absolute Error (MAE), showcasing its capability to manage large-scale and dynamic EV fleets effectively. EcoSwarm is highly scalable and adaptable, making it suitable for addressing challenges in large-scale EV fleet management. Future research will explore its application in real-time autonomous fleet management, optimization systems, and smart grids as integral components of sustainable mobility solutions.

articleTitle: An Integrated Energy Planning Simulation Method Considering the Peak and Valley Regulation Effects of the Storage
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: The stable operation of the new power system with the high proportions of new energy and electronic device has been greatly challenged in recent years. In this context, rational planning and configuration of the system plays an important role in promoting the synergistic development of source-grid-load-storage and ultimately guaranteeing the safe operation of the system. Hourly production and operation simulation is a necessary method for system planning simulation. On the basis of the balance between supply and demand, taking into account the actual operating characteristics of various sources and the regulation effect of pumping and storage units, this paper proposes a combinatorial algorithm for the production and operation simulation of an integrated energy system with the goal of minimizing the operating cost of the system. First of all, the composition of the integrated energy system is clarified and the regulation effect of the pumping and storage units are analyzed. Besides, the model of the production and operation simulation is established by proposing the objective function and operating constraints. On this basis, a combined production operation simulation method based on empirical and heuristic algorithms is proposed, in which the initial solution is obtained by calling process of different sources based on experience, and the final result is further optimized by Gurobi. Finally, an example is used to verify the effectiveness of the method proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Environmental Regulation and Wind Power Generation: Empirical Analysis Based on Provincial Panel Data
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Environmental regulation, as the “visible hand,” still requires further exploration regarding its influence on the development of the wind power industry. Based on theoretical analysis, this paper conducts regression analysis on empirical data from 30 Chinese provinces from 2011 to 2022 using a bidirectional fixed effects panel model. The study finds that: (1) Environmental regulation significantly promotes the development of the wind power industry, and this conclusion remains valid after robustness testing; (2) Wind speed, carbon emissions, patent numbers, and enterprise ownership structures all have a positive impact on the development of the wind power industry, whereas economic development levels and research funding have a certain negative impact; (3) Over time, especially after 2019, the promotion effect of environmental regulation on the wind power industry has significantly increased.

articleTitle: A Study on Grid Coupling-based Big Data Clustering Method for Massive Electricity Carbon Emission with Mixed Attributes
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: To comprehensively and stably categorize and analyze the power carbon emission data for different sizes and types of power carbon emission datasets, a clustering method based on grid coupling is studied for massive power carbon emission big data with mixed attributes. In the offline stage, based on the updated core grid and the center of mass of the grid, we search for grids that are connected with the density, complete the clustering, and obtain the clustering results of the massive electricity carbon emission mixed-attribute big data clustering. It is proved that the method can effectively divide the spatial grid of massive electricity carbon emission mixed-attribute big data and calculate the weight of each data sample, and can quickly cluster massive electricity carbon emission mixed-attribute big data. Under different degrees of interference information, the clustering of the method has a higher normalized mutual information (NMI) index and Riese’s (RI) index, that is, the clustering accuracy is higher.

articleTitle: Exploring Heterogeneous Behaviors in Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) Participation: Perspectives on Influencing Factors and Discharge Pricing
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: As the global energy structure transitions toward low-carbon and sustainable models, the new energy power system faces the structural supply-demand imbalance challenge. At the same time, the rapid development of electric vehicles (EVs) presents new opportunities for enhancing smart grid systems. Through Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology, bidirectional energy flow between EVs and the grid can provide flexible regulation resources to alleviate supply-demand discrepancies. However, the large-scale employment of V2G faces significant barriers in terms of user participation, primarily due to the uncertainty and heterogeneity of EV owners’ participation behavior. To this end, this paper utilizes survey data and applies factor analysis and multiple linear regression to investigate the heterogeneous behavior of EV owners. The research findings reveal significant heterogeneity in influencing factors and discharge pricing. Initially, four core elements-technology awareness, social policy incentives, non-economic benefits, and personal economic gains—affect V2G participation to varying degrees across different regions and occupational groups. Subsequently, discharge pricing exhibits heterogeneous price sensitivity between different regions and occupational groups, with private-sector employees being more price-sensitive than public-sector employees. Based on these findings, the paper proposes differentiated promotion strategies for V2G projects, fostering collaborative development of smart grids and the electric vehicle market.

articleTitle: Research on Line Fault Protection Methods for Three-Terminal High Voltage Direct Current Transmission Systems Based on Voltage Source Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: In recent years, high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission systems based on voltage source converters (VSC) have emerged as a prominent and widely discussed solution for integrating large-scale onshore wind farms into the power grid. These systems have gained significant attention due to their ability to efficiently transmit large amounts of renewable energy over long distances with minimal losses. The VSC-HVDC technology offers several advantages, including flexible power control, the ability to connect to weak AC grids, and the capacity to maintain stable operation even under varying power flow conditions. As the demand for renewable energy integration grows, VSC-HVDC systems have become a key focus in the development of modern power grids, providing a reliable and effective means of harnessing and delivering wind energy to meet increasing electricity demands. Protecting against DC faults in multi-terminal VSC-HVDC networks presents significant difficulties. This study examines the behavior of fault currents in a three-terminal VSC-HVDC setup, where currents can surge dramatically within milliseconds during transient events like capacitor discharge and diode freewheeling following a DC fault. A novel approach for detecting and isolating DC line faults from one end in such three-terminal systems is introduced. This method employs an under-voltage criterion to effectively differentiate between fault states and normal operating conditions in the system. By connecting a DC reactor to remain within the operational capacity range of the circuit breaker, thereby preventing damage to the system components. Additionally, the method provides a recommended range of inductance values for the current-limiting reactor, ensuring optimal performance under various fault scenarios. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed protection scheme, the PSCAD/EMTDC simulation software is utilized to simulate. The simulation results demonstrate the accuracy and reliability of the proposed scheme, confirming its ability to correctly identify and respond to faults while maintaining system stability and protecting critical equipment. This approach offers a robust solution for enhancing the protection of multi-terminal VSC-HVDC systems.

articleTitle: Recent progress of three-dimensional current collector for lithium metal battery
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Lithium metal battery has become a research hotspot due to its high capacity for energy, light weight and extended battery life. However, issues with the lithium metal anode include lithium dendrite growth, unstable solid electrolyte interface (SEI) and volume variation. Three-dimensional current collector materials have attracted wide attention because they can effectively alleviate these problems. First, the growth of the lithium dendrite and the impact of SEI are covered in the mechanism of lithium metal electrodeposition. Subsequently, the latest progress of three-dimensional carbon-based, metal-based and composite current collector materials is reviewed in detail. These materials’ large specific surface area, even charge distribution, and increased lithium affinity have all greatly enhanced the electrochemical performance of the lithium metal anode. In addition, the strategy of modifying the threedimensional current collector by increasing lithium affinity sites and inducing uniform nucleation is presented. Lastly, the forthcoming development direction of three-dimensional current collector materials for lithium metal batteries is prospected.

articleTitle: Study on the Influencing Factors of Carbon Emission Reduction in China in the Context of Globalization
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Smart Grid and Green Energy (ICSGGE)
abstract: Against the backdrop of global climate change and the transition to a low-carbon economy, carbon emission reduction has become a core issue for countries to realize sustainable development. Globalization has brought advanced carbon emission reduction experience to China, which has effectively enhanced China’s carbon emission reduction efficiency. Based on the background of globalization, this paper analyzes in depth the main influencing factors of carbon emission in China, including industrial structure, power generation structure and the guiding role of the government. The study shows that optimization of industrial structure and cleaner power generation structure are the key paths to promote carbon emission reduction, while the government’s policy guidance plays an indispensable role in the low-carbon transition. In order to further enhance the effect of carbon emission reduction, this paper puts forward three suggestions: first, accelerate the industrial structure adjustment and promote the transformation and upgrading of high-energy-consuming industries; second, optimize the power generation structure and increase the proportion of clean energy; and third, strengthen the government’s guiding and supervisory efforts to ensure the effective.
